generatedProse.concept-context: Picture a presentation on a sport-science topic, such as a training method or a match analysis. You decide your one message, structure the talk around it, and design slides that support it, in one connected effort. The thread holding the three ideas together is the audience and the single point you want them to take away.
generatedProse.worked-example: Two sport-science students present the same match analysis. One loads the slides with every statistic and reads them aloud, with no clear message, so the audience cannot see the point. The other decides one message, such as why possession mattered, structures the talk around it, and uses slides that show only the key figures. The second student's audience follows the analysis, because the parts worked as one practice.
generatedProse.summary: In sport science, a presentation works when its message, structure and slides serve one goal. You pick the point that matters, shape the talk around it, and let the slides support it rather than crowd it. As one practice, the three ideas carry your audience through the analysis, not just the numbers.

check.body: A student works out one clear message, plans an introduction, main body and conclusion around it, and builds slides that support it. The talk lands well. What does this show?

items.text: Their next round of learning and preparation, which is why the following programme improved.
Nothing; feedback comes at the end, so it cannot affect anything that follows.
Only the mark on the first programme, which cannot now change.
The deadline for the next programme.

feedback.correct: That's right. Using the feedback fed back into the next round of learning and preparation, which is why the following programme improved: that is the cycle working.
feedback.incorrectNotFinal: Not quite. Think about what the student changed before the next programme, not the old mark or the deadline.
feedback.incorrectFinal: Using the feedback fed back into the student's next round of learning and preparation, which is why the next programme improved. The old mark cannot change and the deadline is not part of the cycle; feedback is not the end, it feeds the next turn.

_items.text: That building a presentation works as one practice: the message, the structure and the slides all pulled the same way.
_items.feedback: Yes. The three parts worked together towards one clear message, which is the whole practice.

_items.text: That the slides were the only thing that mattered.
_items.feedback: The slides helped, but only because they supported a clear message and a sound structure.

_items.text: That the student was lucky, and planning made no difference.
_items.feedback: Planning shaped the talk. The parts working together are what made it land.

_items.text: That a clear message on its own is enough, without structure or slides.
_items.feedback: The message mattered, but the structure and slides carried it. All three worked together.
